groupers.name: GROUP_CATEGORY
groupers.description: Partition records by exact field value; ideal for categorical fields.

keys.name: total_n
keys.description: Total records partitioned across all buckets (post-filter).

keys.name: n_null
keys.description: Records that landed in the null/skip path (no bucket assignment).

keys.name: dict_size
keys.description: Number of distinct values observed across all buckets (cardinality of the partition key).

keys.description: Per-bucket records, ordered by emission; each entry carries {key, label, count}.

groupers.name: GROUP_DATE
groupers.description: Partition date-typed records by a calendar component (year, quarter, month, week, day, hour, hour_of_day, day_of_week). A datetime field is read on the local wall clock of its resolved zone (UTC by default): its calendar day, or for component=hour / hour_of_day its wall-clock hour (datetime only). Keys emit chronologically; day_of_week Monday to Sunday, hour_of_day 00 to 23. Group.Include restricts the keys and sets their order. Optional week_start picks the day a week begins; optional fiscal_offset shifts year/quarter bucketing onto a fiscal calendar with end-year labels (FY-prefixed keys).

params.name: week_start
params.description: Day a week bucket begins on; valid only with component=week. monday (default) keeps ISO-8601 week keys (2026-W09); any other day keys a week by the date of its first day (2026-03-01), and period_start / period_end follow it.

params.name: fiscal_offset
params.description: Months after January when the fiscal year starts; valid only with component=year or component=quarter. Range [-11, 11]; offsets normalise mod 12 (offset=-3 == offset=9 => October start). 0 (default) = calendar year. Non-zero offsets prefix keys with FY using the end-year convention (Apr 2024-Mar 2025 with offset=3 => FY2025).

groupers.emits_type_note: string group key per row (e.g. 2024-Q1, 2024-01, FY2025-Q1, 2026-W09, 2026-03-29T03, Monday, 09)

keys.name: total_n
keys.description: Total records partitioned across all buckets (post-filter).

keys.name: n_null
keys.description: Records that landed in the null/skip path (no bucket assignment).

keys.name: granularity
keys.description: Calendar component used to bucket (hour, hour_of_day, day, day_of_week, week, month, quarter, year).

keys.name: range_start
keys.description: ISO date string of the earliest period observed (YYYY-MM-DDTHH for component=hour).

keys.name: range_end
keys.description: ISO date string of the latest period observed (YYYY-MM-DDTHH for component=hour).

keys.name: n_buckets
keys.description: Number of distinct calendar buckets observed.

keys.name: buckets
keys.description: Per-bucket records, ordered by emission; each entry carries {key, period_start, period_end, count}.

tests.name: TEST_CHISQ
tests.description: Chi-square independence test on a 2D Rows×Cols contingency table; with params.expected and no Cols, a goodness-of-fit test of Rows' level counts against expected proportions.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

params.name: expected
params.description: Goodness of fit: map of Rows level to expected proportion (each > 0, summing to 1 within 1e-9; never renormalised). Selects Variant goodness_of_fit (df = labels − 1) and requires Cols absent; an observed level it omits is refused, a listed level never observed counts as 0.

tests.name: TEST_T
tests.description: One-sample or two-sample Welch t-test on a numeric Field; SplitBy switches to the two-sample variant.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

params.name: mu
params.description: Hypothesized mean for the one-sample variant (ignored when SplitBy is set).

params.name: reference
params.description: SplitBy level read second, so diff, its interval, the statistic and the signed effect size read other − reference (default: alphabetical). A split_by level ("0" / "1" on a packed_bool) and needs SplitBy, else PULSE_TEST_REFERENCE_INVALID; neither observed group is PULSE_TEST_REFERENCE_MISSING.

params.name: covariate
params.description: Numeric pre-period column (CUPED): the test runs on y − θ·(x − x̄), θ the slope of Field on it pooled over both groups, so diff, its interval, the statistic, p and cohens_d are adjusted; details add diff_unadjusted, theta, covariate_mean, variance_reduction, n_covariate_dropped (null-covariate rows dropped). Needs SplitBy; else, or non-numeric, PULSE_TEST_COVARIATE_INVALID — as on any other test.

tests.name: TEST_WELCH
tests.description: Explicit two-sample Welch t-test alias; identical to TEST_T with SplitBy.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Significance level in (0, 1); RejectNull is true when PValue < alpha.

params.name: reference
params.description: SplitBy level read second, so diff, its interval, the statistic and the signed effect size read other − reference (default: alphabetical). A split_by level ("0" / "1" on a packed_bool) and needs SplitBy, else PULSE_TEST_REFERENCE_INVALID; neither observed group is PULSE_TEST_REFERENCE_MISSING.

params.name: covariate
params.description: Numeric pre-period column (CUPED): the test runs on y − θ·(x − x̄), θ the slope of Field on it pooled over both groups, so diff, its interval, the statistic, p and cohens_d are adjusted; details add diff_unadjusted, theta, covariate_mean, variance_reduction, n_covariate_dropped (null-covariate rows dropped). Needs SplitBy; else, or non-numeric, PULSE_TEST_COVARIATE_INVALID — as on any other test.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_errors_lookup
mcp_tools.description: CALL WHEN A TOOL RETURNS AN ERROR CODE YOU NEED EXPLAINED. Look up Pulse error code metadata. Pass code=PULSE_XXX for full detail on one code. Pass domain=PULSE/ENCODING/PROCESSING/SERVICE/DATA/CLI to enumerate that domain. Pass query="text" for keyword search across descriptions and fixups. The manifest carries only the code-name list — fetch detail here on demand to keep session context lean.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_examples_get
mcp_tools.description: CALL AFTER A SEARCH FINDS A MATCHING EXAMPLE, TO GET ITS RUNNABLE BODY. Fetch one request example from the request-example library by `name`. Returns the full record including `body`, a runnable types.Request JSON with the _meta annotation block stripped. Hand it straight to pulse_predict or pulse_process. Serves the same library as pulse_examples_search: embedder examples included, an example that uses a feature this server hides reads as not found.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_examples_search
mcp_tools.description:
CALL BEFORE AUTHORING A REQUEST. Search the request-example library to find a runnable template that matches the user's question. Returns lightweight summaries (name, category, tags, operators, description, intents); fetch the runnable JSON body via pulse_examples_get and modify field names for the target cohort.

The `compose` examples show a compose `sweep` expanded into slots.

The library is this server's own: the shipped examples plus any the embedder registered, minus any that use a feature this server hides (those read as absent).

Prefer this over inferring request shapes from documentation or source code — the shipped examples are curated, runnable, and stay in lockstep with the operator surface; embedder examples are validated the same way at startup.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_facet
mcp_tools.description: CALL TO LIST THE DISTINCT VALUES OF ONE FIELD. Diagnostic / discovery tool — for example, run it before authoring a FILTER_INCLUDE. For multi-field summaries with counts, null tallies, numeric stats, percentiles, histograms, or additive contribution counts, prefer pulse_facet_schema.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_facet_schema
mcp_tools.description: CALL TO SUMMARISE SEVERAL FIELDS AT ONCE WITH COUNTS, NULLS, STATS OR HISTOGRAMS. Multi-field rich facet endpoint. Returns per-field summaries (discrete value/count lists with null tallies for categorical/boolean/geo fields; streaming statistics — count, sum, min, max, mean, stddev — for numeric fields), with optional NumericPercentiles (forces buffered per-field sort), IncludeHistogram + HistogramRange + HistogramBins for fixed-width binning, DiscreteTopK truncation, and AdditiveFields contribution counts that strip the field's own filter clauses so the LLM/UI can report 'if I added value V to my filter on F, this is the population that survives'. Filterers reuse the standard FILTER_* surface. Use this instead of repeated pulse_facet calls when summarising more than one field, when you need counts (not just distinct values), or when building a faceted UI.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_inspect
mcp_tools.description:
CALL TO SEE A COHORT'S FIELDS AND TYPES WITHOUT RUNNING A REQUEST. Read header and schema of a .pulse file without touching record data. Returns the field list (name, type, nullable, dictionary contents for categorical fields), record count, and format metadata.

record_count is DERIVED (payload bytes / record stride), so a cohort whose payload is not a whole multiple of the stride reports the FLOOR. That case carries a coded ENCODING_INVALID entry in the additive `warnings` array with record_stride and trailing_bytes in its details; a clean read emits no `warnings` key at all. Read it — a truncated tail is invisible in the count itself.

Optional `joins` [{right, as}] names the cohorts later requests join: on a server binding tools on inspect, the rebound request tools' field enums add each target's joined names (as + field) and joins[].on[].right_field its fields. Inspect output is unchanged.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_manifest
mcp_tools.description:
CALL FIRST IN EVERY SESSION. The LLM-authored-request bootstrap blob.

WORKFLOW: call once at session start, cache the result, reference it for every subsequent request-authoring decision. This is the source of truth for what operators exist in this Pulse deployment — do NOT infer operator names, param shapes, or accepted types from external documentation or source code. Pair with pulse_examples_search to find runnable templates for the question you are answering.

Pass `intent` (an intent-taxonomy ID such as `compare_groups`) for a manifest scoped to that intent, a small fraction of the size: only operators serving it, its ranked skills and the intent record under `scope`; the fixed sections (commands, error codes, cohort types, tool list, limits, ...) are dropped and named in `elided`. Cache it per intent. An unknown one is PULSE_RECOMMEND_INTENT_UNKNOWN.

MCP always returns the slim payload (no prose descriptions); fetch per-operator prose via pulse_skills_get and per-error prose via pulse_errors_lookup when needed.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_predict
mcp_tools.description: CALL BEFORE STORING OR EXECUTING A HAND-AUTHORED OR GENERATED REQUEST. Validate a processing request against a cohort schema without executing. Returns the same diagnostics execution would emit on shape error (PULSE_REQUEST_UNKNOWN_FIELD, PULSE_FIELD_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED, etc.) plus the normalized request, streamability flag, and the defaults the engine applied; the coded `errors` / `warnings` behind a `valid: false` ride beside the result at the root. Cheap: it reads only the cohort header + schema. To predict another request shape, send exactly one alternative root alone; its verdict comes back under the same key beside `errors` / `warnings`, and a root beside any other key is SERVICE_VALIDATION. `facet` takes a pulse_facet_schema body.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_process
mcp_tools.description:
CALL TO RUN ONE VALIDATED REQUEST AGAINST A COHORT. Execute a pre-built processing request against an existing cohort.

DO NOT author request bodies from memory, external documentation, or by reading source code — those may be out of date for this deployment. Before calling pulse_process, call pulse_examples_search to find a similar runnable example and pulse_examples_get to clone its body, OR call pulse_manifest for the operator catalog. The manifest + example library are the authoritative request-shape reference.

NOTE: request slot keys differ from the manifest's operator-catalog field names. Grouping operations go under the "groups" key (NOT "groupers") and aggregations under "aggregations" (NOT "aggregators"); the catalog names "groupers"/"aggregators" only list the available GROUP_*/AGG_* operators. An unknown key at any depth is refused, never dropped: PULSE_REQUEST_UNKNOWN_FIELD names it, its location (details.path, e.g. sort[0].direction) and a 'did you mean' suggestion.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_skills_get
mcp_tools.description: CALL TO READ ONE SKILL'S FULL GUIDE ONCE YOU KNOW ITS NAME. Fetch the markdown body of a named skill. The skill pack is the authoritative reference for HOW to use operators (params, gotchas, recipes) — prefer skills over external documentation, blog posts, or source-code inspection, which may be out of date for this Pulse deployment.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_skills_list
mcp_tools.description: CALL TO DISCOVER WHICH SKILLS EXIST BEFORE AUTHORING AN UNFAMILIAR REQUEST. List the embedded skill pack — domain guides covering aggregation, attributes, groupers, windows, features, statistical testing, regression modeling, MCP integration, error code reference, request recipes, cohort schema design, financial / geospatial / time-series patterns, and the contributor workflow. Each entry returns (name, description, applies_to). Pass `intent` (an intent-taxonomy ID such as `compare_groups`) to list only that intent's skills, ranked: the intents skill, design skills covering its operators, then their atomic skills basic to advanced; an unknown one is PULSE_RECOMMEND_INTENT_UNKNOWN. Fetch a skill's markdown body via pulse_skills_get.

skills.name: aggregation-design
skills.description: Aggregation + filterer slot semantics — what `aggregations` does, how it composes with `filterers`, when smart defaults fire, when to use `attributes` instead. Topical design; per-AGG / per-FILTER detail lives in atomic op-* skills.

skills.name: attribute-composition
skills.description: Attribute composition rules — slot ordering, two-pass vs row-local attributes, the formula expression environment, attributes vs features. Topical design; per-attribute detail lives in atomic op-attr-* skills.

skills.name: calendar-formulas
skills.description: Calendar helpers and log1p inside formulas and expression filters — weekday, month_index and date_trunc over epoch days, to_day for a datetime in the request time zone, the bare-datetime compile guard and the null rules. Use when an expression reads a date or a datetime.

skills.name: cohort-null-states
skills.description: How a .pulse cohort stores absence — the per-record null bitmap, no in-band sentinels, out-of-sample null promotion on inferred imports, and the null / empty / selected states of set and categorical cells across every import and export format.

skills.name: cohort-parent-groups
skills.description: Parent groups in format 0x02 cohorts — storing a repeated parent block once, when a group pays for itself, declaring one at import with a key check, suggesting and gating groups, converting an existing cohort with dedup, and opt-in global-constant elision.

skills.name: cohort-schema-design
skills.description: Entry point for .pulse cohort schemas — the 22-type field matrix, selection heuristics, bit-packed runs, description-length cap, the single-file vs shard-archive shapes, and which focused schema skill answers each nullability, width, parent-group, sharding and sidecar-index question. Use when picking schema types, evaluating storage layout, or interpreting a cohort returned by pulse_inspect.

skills.name: cohort-sharding
skills.description: Shard archives in depth — strict structural cohesion, dictionary union-merge, set-rung auto-widen on create and add, grouped shards, the anchor syntax, union-wide memory for materializing operations, single-writer concurrency, and transport-only compression for moving a cohort.

skills.name: cohort-sidecar-index
skills.description: The sidecar point-lookup index beside a cohort — the v3 file format, the O(1) seek path, three-outcome staleness, discovery through the indexes.json manifest, invalidation by a cohort rewrite, keyable types, shard-archive indexes and constraints.

skills.name: cohort-width-overflow
skills.description: What happens when a value outgrows its field width — inferred categorical and numeric rungs promote on the full row pass, declared widths refuse row by row, set cardinality and shard dictionary overflow, and how convert reports it.

skills.name: crosstab-guide
skills.description: Crosstab slot — rows × columns groupers, margins-from-raw-rows, normalize / normalize_level / normalize_within, matrix vs long, fused vs buffered, CrosstabComponents indexing. Topical; per-aggregator/grouper math lives in op-* atomics.

skills.name: crosstab-margin-aggregations
skills.description: Auxiliary margin-only figures on a crosstab — a second base beside the cell metric in one scan, the cell-admission rule, present semantics and the display-flag gate

skills.name: decimal-formulas
skills.description: Exact decimal128 arithmetic inside formulas and expression filters — operator result scales, the numeric built-ins over a decimal (abs, round, max, mean and the rest), ternary and ?? lifting, the float() escape, and what is refused at compile. Use when an expression reads a money field.

skills.name: expression-language
skills.description: The per-row expression environment shared by the formula attribute and the expression filter — field binding by type, operators, built-in functions, set helpers, null handling, embedder functions and lookup tables. Not request templating.

skills.name: facet-design
skills.description: FacetSchema endpoint — per-field summaries, histograms, additive contribution counts, streamability tradeoffs, four FACET-host overlay kinds against Population. Per-OVERLAY math in op-overlay-* atomics.

skills.name: feature-engineering
skills.description: Feature slot semantics — choosing a transform, pre-filter ordering (features run before filters), per-row vs global-pass cost, target-leakage trap, train/test split. Topical design; per-feature detail lives in atomic op-feat-* skills.

skills.name: financial-cohorts
skills.description: decimal128 patterns — precision/scale propagation, banker's rounding, divide-by-zero policy, currency conventions, three consumer-facing decimal error codes. Use when a cohort has monetary fields or a response carries PULSE_DECIMAL_OVERFLOW / PULSE_PRECISION_LOSS / PULSE_DECIMAL_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO.

skills.name: glossary
skills.description: Plain-language glossary of the statistical terms Pulse guidance uses. Use when a result, purpose or skill names a term you need explained.

skills.name: grouper-design
skills.description: Grouper slot semantics — multi-grouper composition (key product), fused crosstab eligibility, Group.Include inclusion-list, smart defaults per field type. Topical design; per-GROUP detail lives in atomic op-group-* skills.

skills.name: import-schema-rows
skills.description: Importing a tabular source — an explicit schema matched by column name and its refusal codes, what inference decides (float width, nullability, widths, blank cells), zero-row and partial row failures, format dispatch, compressed and .pulse sources, and the one JSON casing. Topical design; the managed-import tool's own arguments in its atomic skill.

skills.name: import-source-zones
skills.description: Importing naive datetimes recorded in a local zone — source_tz, per-column and per-row (source_tz_field) zones, the DST gap / overlap policy, which native Arrow, Parquet and SPSS timestamps move, the dropped-row and zone warnings, and why a managed handle is re-imported to change zone. Topical design; request-time zones in time-zones.

skills.name: intents
skills.description: The closed intent taxonomy: the kinds of question an analysis answers, how each sounds, and the field shapes it fits. Use to map a user's question to an intent ID.

skills.name: op-group-date
skills.description: Partition date/datetime records by calendar component (hour..year); week_start picks the week day; fiscal_offset shifts year/quarter.

skills.name: op-overlay-index-vs-margin
skills.description: Per-cell index against the matching axis margin (100 × cell / margin).

skills.name: op-overlay-pairwise-welch-t
skills.description: Intra-matrix axis-pairwise Welch–Satterthwaite t-test on AGG_WELFORD cells.

skills.name: op-overlay-share-of-row
skills.description: Per-cell share-of-row ratio (cell / row_margin) — raw share, sums to 1.0 per row.

skills.description: Chi-square independence test on a 2D Rows × Cols contingency table, or goodness of fit of Rows against expected proportions.

skills.name: op-test-t
skills.description: One-sample or two-sample Welch t-test on a numeric field; SplitBy switches to the two-sample variant.

skills.name: op-test-welch
skills.description: Explicit two-sample Welch t-test on a numeric field across a categorical SplitBy partition.

skills.name: overlay-pairwise
skills.description: The contract shared by every intra-crosstab pairwise overlay kind — spec, the pair × opposite-axis p grid, the letters part, missing and degenerate pairs, weighted legs, proportion-cell versus moment-cell hosts and fusion.

skills.name: overlay-reference-tests
skills.description: The contract shared by the inferential overlays that test a figure against a reference — the Compose parity tests (per cell, per group) and their explicit-moments rule, and the prior-period tests on an ordered series — host refusals, missing and degenerate entries, weighted legs.

skills.name: overlay-system
skills.description: Overlay framework — OverlaySpec composition, reference families, three payload shapes, host-arm wiring (SERIES / MATRIX_RESULT / FACET / CHAIN / FORMULA), named payload parts of multi-output kinds. Per-kind detail lives in op-overlay-* atomics.

skills.name: pairwise-n-sources
skills.description: The sample-size vocabulary shared by every OVERLAY_PAIRWISE_* kind — the nine n_source modes, the three distinct-key modes and their cell-aggregator admission, the slab partition gate, the null rules, and p_source.

skills.name: predict-advisories
skills.description: Predict advisories — coded, non-blocking notes in a predict result that the chosen analysis may not fit the data (a two-group test over many groups, many uncorrected p-values, an SPSS nominal or ordinal field treated as a quantity, an unused SPSS weight, Compose p-values split across families, a leave-one-out jackknife over a large cohort, a lasso fit with no valid standard errors); how they differ from warnings, what each code means, what it suggests, and how an embedder suppresses one.

skills.name: regression-inference
skills.description: Coefficient confidence intervals (ci_lower / ci_upper at conf_level) and the coefficient covariance and correlation on a regression — the per-family critical value, the opt-in vcov flag, where each engine's and modifier's matrix comes from, how it relates to the standard errors, weighted fits, the refusals, and what R's vcov does differently. Topical design; per-model params in atomic op-reg-* skills.

skills.name: regression-model-options
skills.description: Model options beyond the textbook fit — ridge over a predictor subset (unpenalized), non-negative coefficients (NNLS), per-coefficient prior precision for an experiment-centred prior, the media-mix recipe, and a regression an embedder registered (params, outputs, what it declines). Topical design; per-model params in atomic op-reg-* skills.

skills.name: regression-modeling
skills.description: Choosing and composing a regression — outcome type, priors, penalties, the resampling and stepwise modifiers, polynomial terms built upstream, and how textbook regression names map to specs. Topical design; per-model detail in atomic op-reg-* skills.

skills.name: regression-row-scores
skills.description: Per-row regression columns — the two-pass refit the fitted, residual and leverage attributes run, scoring a bound fit with params.fit instead, the scoring rule and its refusals, why the fit's predictor list is authoritative, a registered model's scorer, and the save-then-load recipe. skills.name: session-skill-routing

skills.name: spss-cohorts
skills.description: Entry point for SPSS .sav / .zsav cohorts — the three surprises (extra derived columns, codes-not-labels dictionaries, the label-tables directory trap), why dictionaries hold codes, and which focused SPSS skill answers each import, missing-value, sidecar and .sav-writing question. Read this when a cohort came from SPSS or when emitting a .sav.

skills.name: spss-export-fidelity
skills.description: How far the .sav round-trip claim is proven — what CI gates, what was checked only locally against independent readers, what nothing corroborates — and the write-side charset rules (source charset kept, no replacement characters, no silent truncation, encode-measure-segment).

skills.name: spss-export-values
skills.description: What a .sav export writes for each value — the variable-name policy and --sanitize-names, set_* masks at every width, the missing state each null takes, original codes versus dictionary positions, byte order, and labels that live only on user-missing codes.

skills.name: spss-import-schema
skills.description: How a .sav / .zsav file imports — the declared dictionary replaces inference, the SPSS-to-Pulse type mapping, the three data encodings, charset and byte-order rules, and the fatal-vs-warning damage diagnostics. Read this when an SPSS import types a column unexpectedly or refuses a file.

skills.name: spss-metadata-sidecar
skills.description: The cohort.pulse.spss.json sidecar an SPSS import writes — what it records that the .pulse format cannot, the code-label-dictionary-ID triple labels come from, its fingerprint, and the absent / stale / invalid / ignored read verdicts.

skills.name: spss-missing-values
skills.description: How SPSS user-missing and system-missing values land in a cohort — the numeric <var>_missing sibling versus the flagged categorical code, why the two arms deliberately differ, --spss-missing, and filtering on the code rather than the label.

skills.name: spss-response-sets
skills.description: SPSS multiple-response sets and the columns an import synthesises — the derived set_* mask beside a multiple-dichotomy set's constituents, why multiple-category sets derive nothing, and the closed derived registry the export folds by. facet.name: facet_schema
streamable_conditions: NumericPercentiles is empty (percentiles force a buffered per-field value slice + sort)
IncludeHistogram=false OR HistogramRange supplies caller-known [min, max] bounds

crosstab.name: crosstab
streaming_exceptions: shape=long with margins.rows / margins.columns / margins.grand all false and normalize=none streams through the standard grouped path
rejection_rules: crosstab requires at least one grouper in rows (PULSE_CROSSTAB_EMPTY_ROWS)
crosstab requires a cell aggregation — cell, or several measures in cells (PULSE_CROSSTAB_MISSING_CELL)
crosstab cannot coexist with top-level groups or aggregations (PULSE_CROSSTAB_CONFLICTS_WITH_GROUPS)
matrix shape, any margin, or any normalization forces the buffered path
normalize_level_rules: normalize_level must be in [0, len(axis)-1] for the axis selected by normalize (PULSE_CROSSTAB_NORMALIZE_LEVEL_OUT_OF_RANGE)
normalize_level requires normalize to be row or column (PULSE_CROSSTAB_NORMALIZE_LEVEL_WITHOUT_NESTED_AXIS)
normalize_level cannot be combined with normalize=total (PULSE_CROSSTAB_NORMALIZE_LEVEL_INCOMPATIBLE)
normalize_within_rules: normalize_within must be in [0, len(other-axis)-1] where other-axis is columns when normalize=row and rows when normalize=column (PULSE_CROSSTAB_NORMALIZE_WITHIN_OUT_OF_RANGE)
normalize_within requires normalize to be row or column (PULSE_CROSSTAB_NORMALIZE_WITHIN_WITHOUT_AXIS)
normalize_within cannot be combined with normalize=total (PULSE_CROSSTAB_NORMALIZE_WITHIN_INCOMPATIBLE)
margin_aggregation_rules: every margin_aggregations entry needs an aggregation type; null entries are refused (PULSE_CROSSTAB_MARGIN_AGG_INVALID)
margin_aggregations effective labels (label, else TYPE_field) must be unique across the slot and distinct from the cell's (PULSE_CROSSTAB_MARGIN_AGG_DUPLICATE_LABEL)

auxiliary figures are emitted only where the margin is DISPLAYED (margins.rows / margins.columns / margins.grand), matching the emission rule the cell aggregator's own margin counts and components follow; declaring margin_aggregations on a section that displays no margin computes them into nowhere — advisory warning, not a refusal (PULSE_CROSSTAB_MARGIN_AGG_UNOBSERVED) — and a normalize direction does not satisfy it, because the margin it requires is a denominator and an auxiliary is never a denominator

overlays.description: Per-cell index score against the matching axis margin: 100 * cell / margin. CELL scope over a MATRIX (crosstab) host with a Margin reference. Honours OverlaySpec Level / Within slots for nested-axis denominator truncation.

Intra-matrix axis-pairwise Welch–Satterthwaite t-test on AGG_WELFORD cells (Welch SE + Satterthwaite df, Student-t tail; reads the {mean, variance, n} Welford triple from CellComponents). A cell whose declared ComponentSchema lacks mean + variance fires PULSE_OVERLAY_REF_INCOMPATIBLE_WITH_SHAPE, at predict and at runtime. n_source and p_source are NOT accepted on this kind: n, mean and variance all come from the triple, so setting either selector was a silent no-op and predict now refuses it with PULSE_OVERLAY_PARAM_MISSING; a distinct-key n_source is refused at runtime too, under that same code. MATRIX payload: the PAIR axis carries one entry per evaluated (i, j) index pair (key = the 2-tuple of the compared legs' labels), the OPPOSITE axis echoes the host's other axis, and each cell holds the pair's two-sided p-value (absent when a leg is unreadable or the test degenerate). The Ref union is left empty (intra-matrix). n_within_distinct sums per-cell cardinalities, so the summed-across pair-axis dims must PARTITION the key set — a fan-out grouper at a depth beyond n_within_depth fires PULSE_OVERLAY_DISTINCT_SLAB_NOT_PARTITIONED at predict AND at runtime, while row_margin_distinct / column_margin_distinct accumulate over raw records and are exact by construction, never gated. Reads Response.Components.Crosstab — a components-disabled host fires PULSE_OVERLAY_COMPONENTS_REQUIRED, at predict and at runtime. RAW p-values; params.letters adds a letters part (per host cell: its letter, comparison group, and the letters it is higher than and significantly above). Buffered (inferential).

params.name: pair_along_dim
params.description: Restrict pairs to pair-axis keys that agree on every dim position except this one; absent = every pair.

params.name: n_within_depth
params.description: With a within-prefix n_source, the pair-axis dim positions (depth + 1) the n denominator is summed within; inert otherwise.

overlays.description: Per-cell share-of-row ratio: cell / row_margin. CELL scope over a MATRIX (crosstab) host. Row cells sum to 1.0 in the absence of missing cells; renderers can present the layer as a 100%-stacked horizontal projection. Honours OverlaySpec Level / Within slots for nested-axis denominator truncation.
